conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: File control entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The SELECT clause shall be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses that follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.2 -> OK §12.4.5.2 1)). Code: fileControlClauseGroup is `SELECT OPTIONAL? (fileName | reservedGatedWord) fileControlClauses* DOT`, and fileControlClauses is a flat alternation (assign, relative key, organization, access mode, record key, record delimiter, alternate key, file status, reserve, padding, sharing, lock mode, collating, unrecognizedClause) so both halves hold structurally: SELECT is the only possible entry opener and every following clause is order-free (ASSIGN included). Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 2023): probe/fce/sr1order (SELECT F1 ORGANIZATION ... ACCESS MODE ... ASSIGN TO last) compiles and runs 'OK' exit 0; probe/fce/sr1nosel (`ASSIGN TO "a.dat" SELECT F1.`) is refused COBOL0001 unexpected 'ASSIGN'. No spec-derived test pins the any-order half by name; test-needed. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the rule is stated for ALL FORMATS of the file control entry; no Annex E row touches it)]
rows.rule-text: The SELECT clause shall be specified first in the file control entry. The clauses that follow the SELECT clause may appear in any order.

rows.subject: File control entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is specified: a) the collating sequence for alphanumeric record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native alphanumeric collating sequence; b) the collating sequence for national record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native national collating sequence.' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 -> OK 6) a)). Code: ResolveFileCollating falls through to native (null weights = ordinal) when no Format-1/Format-2 clause names the key (GR4/GR5 of §12.4.5.7.4 per its doc). Probes (--std 2023): probe/fce/gr6nat_x (alphanumeric prime key, no clause) walks 11, AA, BB, ZZ, aa = native ordinal; probe/fce/gr6pcs_x (same + OBJECT-COMPUTER PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV) walks the SAME native order - the program collating sequence does not leak into key order; probe/fce/gr6nat_n (PIC N(2) prime key) walks native national order; alternate keys: probe/fce/gr6alt_x2 (alphanumeric alternate, PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE REV, START >= spaces) walks 11, AA, BB, ZZ, aa, and probe/fce/gr6alt_n (national alternate) likewise. All four quadrants (primary/alternate x alphanumeric/national) verified. No spec-derived golden pins the no-clause default by name; test-needed. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 per the clause text; b) (national record keys) applies where national data exists (2002+)]
rows.rule-text: If no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is specified: a) the collating sequence for alphanumeric record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native alphanumeric collating sequence; b) the collating sequence for national record keys, both primary and alternate, is the native national collating sequence.

rows.subject: File description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The clauses that follow file-name-1 may appear in any order.' (cite.py --check 13.4.5.3 -> OK §13.4.5.3 2)). Grammar: fileDescriptionClauses : fileDescriptionClause+ (unordered repetition); binder iterates the list order-independently. Probes: probe/fde/sr2_order (FD F RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS LINAGE IS 20 LINES BLOCK CONTAINS 1 RECORDS IS GLOBAL IS EXTERNAL — printed order reversed) compiles, runs, writes; probe/fde/sr2_order_codeset (CODE-SET before RECORD before GLOBAL) compiles and runs. No spec-derived test names this rule. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the file description entry and this rule exist in every edition; no Annex E item touches 13.4.5)
rows.rule-text: The clauses that follow file-name-1 may appear in any order.

rows.subject: File description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes:
Rule constrains the PROGRAMS of a run unit: every FD for one external connector shall agree on BLOCK CONTAINS (a), CODE-SET (b), LINAGE literals/external items (c), smallest/largest record size (d), REPORT presence (e) (cite.py --check 13.4.5.4 'all shall have a BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifying the same minimum and maximum size of the physical record' -> OK §13.4.5.4 2) a)). It is a GENERAL rule with no mandated detection: §4.2.2 'There are general rules in standard COBOL that could have been classified as syntax rules ... An implementation may, but is not required to, flag violations' (cite.py OK §4.2.2) and §4.4 'The results of violating the formats or rules of standard COBOL are undefined' (cite.py OK §4.4 2)); the only mandated EC check, §14.8.4.4, covers the FILE CONTROL entry (12.4.5 GR1), not the FD (cite.py OK §14.8.4.4). So the obligation is that a run unit OBEYING GR2 works. Probed the conforming path: probe/fde/gr2/gr2.cob (two programs, FD XF IS EXTERNAL BLOCK CONTAINS 2 RECORDS RECORD CONTAINS 10 CHARACTERS LINAGE IS 20 LINES CODE-SET IS AL1, identical in both) -> one shared connector, file = 'MAIN1
SUB1
MAIN2
', LINAGE-COUNTER after 3 writes = 0004 (correct, shared page), same at --std 85; probe/fde/gr2/gr2e.cob (e): both describers carry REPORT IS RP on one external FD -> compiles and both programs' report lines reach the one file. LINAGE literal/item sameness (c) is additionally checked at run time via ExternalDescriptor.LinageRef (EC-EXTERNAL-DATA-MISMATCH). Not flagged at compile time within one compilation group: permitted by §4.2.2. ⚠ docs/rearchitecture/PHASE-13-plan-vs-spec-review.md V51 asserts in-group GR2(c) is an 'always-Error requirement' and lists it OPEN in a design doc rather than kb/Work — the spec imposes no such obligation (§4.2.2), see dossier_gaps. Existing golden conformance:2023/pb673_external_assign_executor exercises only GR2 d) of the five items, so it is not named as the closing test. Observation (not this row): in gr2e the first line of each program's report is emitted with no preceding advance ('MAINLINESUBLINE
MAINLINE
'), which is report-writer line framing — the implementor-defined structure of GR-13.4.5.4-4. || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the file description entry and this rule exist in every edition; no Annex E item touches 13.4.5)
rows.rule-text: If the EXTERNAL clause is specified, all file description entries in the run unit that reference the same file connector as file-name shall obey the following rules: a) If any of the file description entries has a BLOCK CONTAINS clause, all shall have a BLOCK CONTAINS clause specifying the same minimum and maximum size of the physical record. b) If any of the file description entries has a CODE-SET clause, all shall have a CODE-SET clause specifying the same character set. c) If any of the file description entries has a LINAGE clause, all shall have a LINAGE clause specifying 1\. the same corresponding values for any literals specified 2\. the same corresponding external data items. d) All file description entries shall have the same smallest and largest record size. e) If any of the file description entries has a REPORT clause, all shall have a REPORT clause. NOTE If a record description entry is not specified for a file description for an external file, the results can be undefined and can result in data corruption.

rows.subject: File description entry
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'If the file description entry for a sequential file contains the LINAGE clause and the EXTERNAL clause, the LINAGE-COUNTER data item is an external data item. If ... the GLOBAL clause, LINAGE-COUNTER is a global name.' (cite.py --check 13.4.5.4 'the LINAGE-COUNTER data item is an external data item' and 'LINAGE-COUNTER is a global name' -> OK §13.4.5.4 3)). Probe probe/fde/gr3/gr3b.cob (2023) and gr3_85.cob (--std 85): outer program FD GF IS GLOBAL LINAGE 20 writes 2 lines, contained program reads LINAGE-COUNTER OF GF = 0003 and unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER after its own WRITE = 0004 (global name resolves in the containee); FD XF IS EXTERNAL LINAGE 20 in two separate programs: main after 3 writes = 0004, called program sees 0004, writes, sees 0005, main after return sees 0005 (one run-unit LINAGE-COUNTER). Both halves verified at 2023 and 85. ⚠ Separate crash found while probing (finding 5): DISPLAY LINAGE-COUNTER [OF f] throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException 'computed expression in a string context' at run time — a DISPLAY operand defect, not this rule's semantics (MOVE LINAGE-COUNTER is correct). || Editions (adjudicator): 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the file description entry and this rule exist in every edition; no Annex E item touches 13.4.5) || Code sites (adjudicator detail): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindLinageClause; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindFileSection (fileGlobalExternalClause arm: IsExternal / IsGlobal)
rows.rule-text: If the file description entry for a sequential file contains the LINAGE clause and the EXTERNAL clause, the LINAGE-COUNTER data item is an external data item. If the file description entry for a sequential file contains the LINAGE clause and the GLOBAL clause, LINAGE-COUNTER is a global name.

rows.subject: File section
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 13.4.2 'constant-entry' -> OK §13.4.2 (General format). Format: FILE SECTION. [ { file-description-entry [constant-entry | record-description-entry | type-declaration-entry] ... } | { sort-merge-file-description-entry { constant-entry | record-description-entry | type-declaration-entry } ... } ] ... Grammar: `fileSection : FILE SECTION DOT (fileDescriptionEntry | sortMergeDescriptionEntry)*`, each entry `FD|SD fileName clauses? DOT dataDescriptionEntry*` where dataDescriptionEntry carries record, constant (01 ... CONSTANT) and TYPEDEF entries. Verified by probe: p1.cob FD with 01 K1 CONSTANT AS 7, 01 T1 TYPEDEF PIC X(3), a record, a trailing constant, then SD with a constant + record, WS item TYPE T1 -> runs K1=7 K2=9 K3=11 W1=ABC at 2002/2014/2023; at 85 the constant and TYPEDEF entries draw COBOLNET0900 (edition gate, correct). p2.cob empty FILE SECTION (outer brackets = optional) compiles and runs at 2023 and 85. p3.cob a level-01 before any FD/SD -> COBOL0001 (not admitted by the format; rejected). FD with zero entries is admitted by the bracket (subject to §13.4.5.3 SR3, a different row; PB345 landed). SD braces (at least one entry) are enforced through §13.4.6.3 SR2 COBOLNET1837 (conformance:negative/pb345-sd-no-record), which is stricter (a record is required) and is SR2's row, not this one. No spec-derived golden writes a constant or type-declaration entry inside the FILE SECTION, so test-ref empty (test-needed). || Editions (adjudicator): FILE SECTION header with FD/SD + record-description entries at 85, 2002, 2014, 2023; the constant-entry and type-declaration-entry alternatives 2002, 2014, 2023 (introduced with the constant entry / TYPEDEF at 2002)
rows.rule-text:
┌ ┌ constant-entry ┐ ┐ │ │ │ │ │ file-description-entry │ record-description-entry │ … │ │ │ │ │ │ └ type-declaration-entry ┘ │ FILE SECTION. │ │ … │ ╭ constant-entry ╮ │ │ │ │ │ │ sort-merge-file-description-entry ┤ record-description-entry ├ … │ │ │ │ │ └ ╰ type-declaration-entry ╯ ┘
> **Figure notes (File section general format).** `FILE` and `SECTION` are underlined in the printed standard (required words). No choice indicators are present. Note the asymmetry, faithfully reproduced from the printed page: the entry group after `file-description-entry` is enclosed in **brackets** (zero or one of the three, repeatable via the following `…`), while the entry group after `sort-merge-file-description-entry` is enclosed in **braces** (exactly one of the three, repeatable). The outer delimiter is a **bracket** followed by `…`, so the whole two-alternative group is optional and may be repeated. where the following meta-language terms are described in the indicated subclauses: | Term | Subclause | |---|---| | constant-entry | 13.10, Constant entry | | record-description-entry | 13.11, Record description entry | | type-declaration-entry | 13.12, Type declaration entry |

rows.subject: File sharing (which devices allow concurrent access to the file)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §9.1.15 (cite.py OK: 'The implementor shall specify which devices allow concurrent access to a physical file'); §14.9.27.4 21) (cite.py OK) 'effective only for files that are shareable'. grep shareable/device in Cobol.Net.Runtime: no device predicate; every connector is arbitrated. Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/d76.cob: ASSIGN PRINTER "d76.prt" OUTPUT 00 plus ASSIGN DISK "d76.prt" EXTEND 00 concurrently (ALL OTHER), both writes land; two ALL OTHER EXTEND on /dev/null 00/00, NO OTHER on it while they are open 61, alone 00. sh78.cob confirms the regular-file arbitration. The cross-run-unit lock strength on Linux/macOS is kb/Work/PB833 (open) and the clause-less default is kb/Work/PB322 A (open). Neither is stated as settled in the row. Row closes PB322 determination B for item 76.
rows.rule-text: File sharing (which devices allow concurrent access to the file). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (9.1.15, Sharing mode)

rows.subject: Files
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (9.1.14 first list item 1): status set to the invalid key value (9.1.13.5) "and, if enabled, the EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY exception condition is set to exist" [cite.py --check PASS 9.1.14]. Two halves, both verified. Status: E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p914\k1.cob at 85/2023 — duplicate WRITE 22, READ/DELETE/START/REWRITE of a missing key 23, each visible in FILE STATUS inside the phrase and after the statement. EC: __IoCheckEc calls ExceptionState.SetIo before the INVALID KEY short-circuit, so the condition exists even when the phrase is written: E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p914\k5.cob (>>TURN EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY CHECKING ON) at 2002/2014/2023: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS inside the INVALID KEY imperative = EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY and inside the USE declarative = EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY; E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p914\k3.cob T6 same inside an exception-checking PERFORM. TEST-NEEDED: the status half is covered by conformance:2023/l1_delete_invalid_key_transfer, but no spec-derived test asserts EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY is set (grep of tests/ finds none). || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 for the I-O status half; the EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY half 2002+ (exception conditions and >>TURN) || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/KeyedIoEmitter.cs (status-first shape: store status then hook then branch); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/SequentialIoEmitter.cs#EmitUseHook; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/EcEmitter.cs#EmitIoCheckEc (ExceptionState.SetIo BEFORE the phrase short-circuits)
rows.rule-text: The I-O status of the file connector associated with the statement is set to a value indicating the invalid key condition as described in 9.1.13.5, Invalid key condition with unsuccessful completion, and, if enabled, the EC-I-O-INVALID-KEY exception condition is set to exist.

rows.subject: Files
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule text (item 4 + the opening sentence of the not-exists paragraph): "If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified ... and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement" and "If the invalid key condition does not exist ... the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified" [cite.py --check PASS 9.1.14]. Two halves, both verified. (a) no phrase, no applicable statement: a declarative-free unit emits no hook (EmitUseHook returns when !UseDecls and no EC mask) and no branch, so control falls to the next statement — probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p914\k6.cob at 85 and 2023 (declarative-free, duplicate-key WRITE with no phrase: NEXT-STMT 22) and k2.cob T5 (the USE ON I-O tier does not apply to a closed file: T5-END 48 with no DECL line). (b) phrase ignored when no invalid key: EmitInvalid runs the INVALID KEY imperative on '2x' only — l1_delete_invalid_key_transfer arm B (NOTINV=00, no INV-B) and arm D ('49' with INVALID KEY written: INV-D absent); probe k1.cob T4/T5. TEST-NEEDED for half (a): every spec-derived 9.1.14 golden carries a USE declarative or writes the phrase; none pins the no-phrase, no-applicable-statement case. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (no Annex E change for these sentences)
rows.rule-text: If the INVALID KEY phrase is not specified in the input-output statement and there are no applicable exception processing statements, control is transferred to the end of the input-output statement. If the invalid key condition does not exist after the execution of the input-output operation specified by an input-output statement, the INVALID KEY phrase is ignored, if specified. The I-O status of the file connector associated with the statement is updated and the following actions occur:

rows.subject: Files
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (9.1.5 item 2): "both programs may refer to a common file connector by referring to an associated global file-name either in the containing program or in any program that directly or indirectly contains the containing program" [cite.py --check PASS 9.1.5]. Probe E:\Temp\claude\E--CobolSharp\a700c052-f9e4-4942-84ff-a13c7505d6ec\scratchpad\adj-d2b\out\probe\p915\g1.cob (2023) / g85.cob (85, EXIT PROGRAM): A declares FD GF GLOBAL, OPENs OUTPUT, writes AAAA, CALLs contained B which WRITEs BBBB (B-W 00) and CALLs C (contained in B, i.e. INDIRECTLY contained in A) which WRITEs CCCC (C-W 00); A CLOSEs, reopens and reads R=AAAA R=BBBB R=CCCC then EOF 10. Same at 85 and 2023 — one common connector across direct and indirect containment. TEST-NEEDED: conformance:85/pb369_global_file_use_selection references the global file-name from B and C but each OPEN fails (35), so it never demonstrates the connector is COMMON; tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Integration/SpecFixTests.NestedProgram_ReadsContainingGlobalIndexedFile_SharesConnector exercises the LEGACY compiler and does not qualify. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (nested programs + GLOBAL are COBOL-85; no Annex E change) || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/BinderDriver.cs (containers' GLOBAL FDs merged into FilesByName); src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/RunUnit.cs#RunUnit
rows.rule-text: If a program is contained within another program, both programs may refer to a common file connector by referring to an associated global file-name either in the containing program or in any program that directly or indirectly contains the containing program.

rows.subject: Fixed file attribute (whether the ability to share a file is a fixed file attribute)
rows.adjudicator-notes: §9.1.6 (cite.py OK: 'The implementor shall specify whether the ability to share a physical file is a fixed file attribute'). The answer NO was previously written only inside the DOC-A.1-129 row; this row files it under its own key. Probe /tmp/adj/doc/doc-w1-s3/probe/sh78.cob (one path, F1 SHARING WITH NO OTHER, F2/F3 SHARING WITH ALL OTHER LOCK MODE MANUAL): OPEN OUTPUT F1 00; OPEN INPUT F2 while F1 open 61; after CLOSE, F2 and F3 INPUT together 00/00; F1 INPUT while they are open 61; F1 alone 00. No spec-derived test pins the not-carried-by-the-file answer; test-ref empty. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534 (item 78).
rows.rule-text: Fixed file attribute (whether the ability to share a file is a fixed file attribute). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (9.1.6, Fixed file attributes)

rows.subject: Fixed-form reference format
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (§6.3.4 3): "All spaces." cite.py --check 6.3.4 "All spaces" -> OK §6.3.4 3). Code: a line shorter than 7 columns becomes an empty output line (AppendLine()). A line whose program-text area is all spaces goes through the default arm: StripInlineComment, then TrimEnd, which gives an empty line. Probe ffp15 has blank lines of 0 characters, 6 spaces, 7 characters, and a sequence number followed by 66 spaces, placed between division headers and inside the PROCEDURE DIVISION. It compiles and prints BLANKS-OK. The all-spaces line breaks only when it falls between the parts of a continued literal (ffp2 crash). That is §6.3.5's interspersing rule and is recorded under SR-6.3.5-1 and SR-6.3.5-2 (finding F1). No spec-derived test targets this row; SourceFormatTests.FixedSegment_TrailingBlankLine_Preserved is a §6.5 line-count test. || Editions (adjudicator, verbatim): 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 || Code sites (adjudicator, verbatim): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Preprocessor/ReferenceFormatProcessor.cs#ConvertFixedToFree (line.Length < SourceAreaStart arm; default arm with an all-space program-text area)
